newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end higher, T-bonds strong.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end higher, T-bonds strong.

text.p: U.S. interest rate futures ended a busy pit session higher, with the long end turning in another strong technical performance as traders also weighed Tuesday's U.S. elections and three-year Treasury note sale.
December T-bond futures firmed again in fairly quiet late trading, with traders noting local and paper buying as the contract returned above the 113-18/32 level.

Traders glossed over 0.2-percent rise in Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook retail sales for October vs September. Nor did traders respond much to a 3.9-percent drop in Ford's October car sales. Ford's vehicle sales rose 2.5 percent.
Instead, they focused on technicals that many said still pointed to higher prices, at least nearterm.
"It was still a pretty impressive market, if you look at it overall," said one bank floor broker.

He said December T-bond futures face the next close-by technical test at the 114-18/32 level, which represents a 61.8-percent retracement of the drop to the 104-31/32 hit on June 13 from 120-15/32, set on January 4.
"If it gets above there, between you and me, it's got to move (higher)," he added.
From there, some looked for a challenge of 115-00 level.
The market barely downticked after the three-year T-note had sold at a average yield of 5.879 percent with a bid/cover ratio of 2.28 and $564 million in non-competitive bids.

Some traders had looked for better results, with a slightly lower yield and stronger retail interest. But the sale seemed overshadowed by a shift in sentiment apparent on Tuesday about expected outcome of U.S. Congressional races.

Several floor brokers noted unconfirmed talk of assorted news letters and election polls that they said suggested to traders the so-called "tax-and-spend" Democrats are not likely to wrest control of Congress from the Republicans.
Several called the rise in T-bond and Eurodollar futures prices a "relief" trade from market election worries that had loomed as recently as last week.
March Eurodollars firmed, with brokers noting good overseas buying, but it stayed shy of resistance at last Friday's high of 94.51, a level where big offers emerged.

December T-bonds ended up 25/32 at 113-25/32, T-notes ended up 13/32 at 110-01/32, munis gained 13/32 to 116-19/32, March T-bills gained four bps to 94.95, and Eurodollars added three bps to 94.46. -Derivatives Desk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
